I've helped build a couple Windows PCs in the past. It's looking like I need to switch to a Linux for my personal system and would like to look at building one.
What are your best resources for building a Linux desktop?
/v/linux and /v/buildapc should be able to help.

Good advice. As far as hardware is concerned though, your choices really shouldn't vary much from Windows (just keep in mind what you'll be using the PC for). It used to be advised to avoid ATI/AMD graphic cards for Linux, but ATI recently upped their game big time and are starting to produce some drivers that are actually good and functional. I think one of the drivers is actually a proprietary/open source mix as well, or something like that.

Edit: If you're looking for advice on software set up or things like that, check out the "Arch Linux" wiki. Even if you're not using Arch, there's a lot of really great guides and advice on those articles.

I believe that AMD still has bad drivers, but don't quote me on that.

Also be sure to look through all of your options, there's quite a few distros that you can use.
The gentoo website used to be very good for this regardless of the distro you chose.

The Gentoo handbook is an incredible resource. I remember when I first got into using Linux in my home I printed off a copy. It took a lot of ink and took a bit of time, but it was worth it. It was very detailed and really gave you insight on what was going on when you were attempting to install Gentoo.

To this day, I think a big part of my Linux knowledge comes from experimenting with Gentoo and following along with the Gentoo handbook.

As for hardware, anything should work.

If you're just getting started, you should use a distro that sets everything up for you. This will provide a good starting point you can use to learn about your system. For this, I recommend Ubuntu, Mint, or Manjaro.

These distros are like the McDonalds cheeseburgers of Linux. They are good for a quick meal, but you don't have much choice over the toppings, and you'll never learn how to cook.

When you are ready for something more powerful, look into ArchLinux or Gentoo.
